findings.title: Crash when Google Meet booking has no destination calendar
findings.body: The code destructures the first element of evt.destinationCalendar and then accesses mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration without optional chaining or a null check. When destinationCalendar is null or an empty array (handleNewBooking explicitly sets it to null when neither the event type nor organizer has one), this throws a TypeError whenever evt.location is Google Meet, aborting EventManager.create instead of falling back to Cal Video as the previous optional-chained code did.

findings.title: Google updateEvent fallback can never find a calendar
findings.body: When externalCalendarId is falsy, selectedCalendar is computed by finding a destination calendar whose externalId equals that same falsy externalCalendarId, which can never match a real calendar id, so selectedCalendar is undefined and calendar.events.update is called with calendarId: undefined. The previous behaviour fell back to the destination calendar's externalId. Legacy bookings and any update path without a stored externalCalendarId will therefore fail to update the Google event. The same dead fallback exists in deleteEvent, which then silently falls back to 'primary' and may delete from the wrong calendar.

findings.title: Secondary hosts' Google events use the main host's calendar as organizer email
findings.body: createEvent always uses the first destination calendar's externalId as the organizer attendee email, even when credentialId identifies a different (secondary collective) host whose calendar is selected via the credentialId lookup below. The secondary host's event is therefore created on their calendar but attributed to the main host's calendar address, which Google can reject or display with the wrong organizer. The organizer email should come from the destination calendar matching the passed credentialId, not destinationCalendar[0]; updateEvent has the same defect.

findings.title: Office365 createEvent ignores credentialId and always uses first host's calendar
findings.body: EventManager now calls createEvent once per destination calendar with that host's credential, but this implementation does not accept/use credentialId and always targets destinationCalendar[0]. For a collective event, the second host's Office365 token is used to POST to /me/calendars/{first host's externalId}/events, which will 404 or create on the wrong calendar, so non-Google collective hosts do not actually receive their event despite the PR's goal. LarkCalendarService and the CalDAV BaseCalendarService have the identical first-element-only pattern.

findings.title: Lark createEvent always uses the main host's calendar id
findings.body: createEvent (and createAttendees) destructure only destinationCalendar[0] and ignore the credential being used. When EventManager iterates to the second collective host and instantiates Lark with that host's credential, it still creates the event and attendees on the first host's Lark calendar id, causing API failures or events on the wrong calendar. It needs the same per-credential destination selection Google received.

findings.title: CalDAV createEvent filters by main host calendar for every host
findings.body: BaseCalendarService.createEvent filters the credential's calendars to the first destination calendar's externalId. For a secondary collective host whose CalDAV account does not contain the main host's calendar, the filter yields zero calendars, Promise.all resolves empty, and the method still returns a fabricated uid as success, so EventManager records a booking reference for an event that was never created on the second host's calendar.

findings.title: Video booking references lose their credentialId
findings.body: referencesToCreate now sets credentialId to undefined for every non-calendar result, whereas previously video results kept result.credentialId. Dedicated video (e.g. Zoom/Daily) booking references are persisted without credentialId, and later flows such as handleCancelBooking only delete the video meeting when bookingVideoReference.credentialId is present, so video meetings for new bookings may leak/not be deleted or updated.

findings.title: References created without externalId in fallback/other-calendar branches
findings.body: In the branches where a destination has no credentialId, where no destination exists, and for the trailing other_calendar credentials (lines 380, 391, 403), createEvent is called without destination.externalId, so CalendarManager returns externalId undefined and the persisted BookingReference has externalCalendarId undefined. Previously references derived externalCalendarId from evt.destinationCalendar. Updates/deletes for those events then depend on the broken per-service fallbacks and can target 'primary' or no calendar instead of the calendar the event was created on.

findings.title: Reschedule merge deletes only the first old calendar event
findings.body: updateAllCalendarEvents now loops over all calendar references for updates, but the newBookingId cleanup still uses booking.references.find(...) and deletes only the first old calendar event. For a collective booking with one reference per host, the other hosts' old events are never deleted when merging into the new booking, leaving orphaned duplicate events on those hosts' calendars after reschedule.

findings.title: Recurring cancellation duplicates deletes with wrong credentials
findings.body: The new outer loop iterates every calendar reference, and inside the recurring/allRemainingBookings branch it again maps over all of the organizer's calendar credentials and, for each updated booking, picks only the first calendar reference via find(). Each recurring event is therefore delete-attempted once per reference times per credential, mostly with a credential that does not own that reference's uid/externalCalendarId. This produces spurious delete failures (and possible wrong-calendar deletions) for collective recurring bookings instead of deleting each reference once with its own credentialId.

findings.title: Confirming a collective booking only creates the organizer's calendar event
findings.body: The evt built for handleConfirmation contains only booking.destinationCalendar or the confirming user's destinationCalendar as a single-element array, with no destination calendars for the other collective hosts. Since EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents now creates events solely by iterating evt.destinationCalendar, a requires-confirmation collective booking that is later confirmed will only create an event for one host, defeating the multi-host fix on the confirmation path. The Stripe/PayPal webhook handlers build the same single-destination evt.

findings.title: Collective team calendars are dropped when organizer has no destination calendar
findings.body: evt.destinationCalendar is set to null when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar, and the collective merge then does evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars). With null, the optional chain silently no-ops, so all collected team hosts' destination calendars are lost and EventManager falls back to the first connected calendar instead of creating an event per host.

findings.title: Unrelated inversion of organization slug assignment
findings.body: This file is unrelated to destination calendars, but the change flips slug assignment from 'slug when team billing is NOT enabled' to 'slug only when team billing IS enabled' (and now sets both slug and requestedSlug in the billing case). Organizations created without team billing will be created without a slug, breaking their org URL/routing, while billing-enabled orgs get a final slug before the requested-slug flow expects it.
